findings.title: Age grim experimental (Results, para 1 / Table 1, Age row)
findings.description: Age is not stated by the paper to be recorded as whole years, so discreteness is ASSUMED, not stated -- this check cannot reach 'impossible' regardless of outcome. An initial pass mistakenly left the tool's default Likert scale_min/max=1-7 in place, which returned a spurious 'out of range' failure -- an artifact of my own tool-call error, not a property of the paper (age is obviously not a 1-7 scale). Rerun with a defensible, logically-necessary human-age bound [0,120]: GRIM has no discriminating power at this n/precision, so the result is indeterminate, not evidence either way.

findings.title: Statcheck no apa stats (Whole text (Results/Discussion))
findings.description: statcheck scans for APA-formatted inline statistics (e.g. chi2(1)=X, p=Y). The paper reports only a bare p-value ("p = 0.639") with no accompanying chi2 statistic or df printed in text, so statcheck's text-pattern scanner finds nothing to parse -- this is a property of the paper's minimal reporting style, not evidence of anything. The chi2 statistic itself was independently recalculated and verified above from the raw counts.

findings.title: Infection case narrative ambiguity (Results, para 2)
findings.description: This is a wording/reporting-clarity issue, not an arithmetic impossibility -- the paper never assigns each of the 4 remaining infected patients to a specific group, so the ambiguity cannot be resolved by any forensic tool. Capped at suspicious per instruction; flagged because it sits in the passage describing the primary outcome (infection counts feeding directly into the headline chi-squared test).

anchors.quote: One patient in the experimental group was diagnosed with an infection by facial swelling, redness and sinus haziness in the waters' view, and the other 4 patients were diagnosed with a postoperative infection by swelling and redness, and pain on the mandibular area.

findings.quote: One patient in the experimental group was diagnosed with an infection by facial swelling, redness and sinus haziness in the waters' view, and the other 4 patients were diagnosed with a postoperative infection by swelling and redness, and pain on the mandibular area.

computed.method: count check by inspection: sentence literally attributes '1 patient' plus 'the other 4 patients' to symptom categories directly following the phrase 'in the experimental group', summing to 5 patients, versus Table 1's stated 3 infections in the experimental group (and 2 in control, total 5).

consequence.explanation: If read literally, this sentence attributes 5 infected patients to the experimental group alone, contradicting the Table 1 / preceding-sentence count of 3 experimental-group infections (and 2 control-group infections, total 5). The more probable reading is that '1 patient' belongs to the experimental group and 'the other 4' are distributed across both groups (2 exp + 2 control, or similar), which would reconcile the totals (1+4=5=3+2), but the sentence as written does not make that split explicit.

findings.notes: This is a wording/reporting-clarity issue, not an arithmetic impossibility -- the paper never assigns each of the 4 remaining infected patients to a specific group, so the ambiguity cannot be resolved by any forensic tool. Capped at suspicious per instruction; flagged because it sits in the passage describing the primary outcome (infection counts feeding directly into the headline chi-squared test).
